best_for: C and C++ developers, including students and hobbyists on the free non-commercial license, who want an IDE that understands CMake projects and runs on Windows, Mac and Linux.

points.title: Free unless you are paid for the code
points.text: CLion has a free non-commercial license for learning, open source, content creation and hobby projects. Commercial work needs a paid subscription, and there is a 30-day trial that needs no login.

points.title: The free license has strings
points.text: It needs a JetBrains Account and an online activation, then renews yearly if you used it in the last six months. It also sends anonymous usage statistics, and you cannot turn that off without a paid license.

points.title: Compilers: Windows ready, Linux not
points.text: On Windows it bundles MinGW, so you can build right away. On a Mac it uses Xcode or the command line tools. On Linux you install GCC or Clang yourself first.

points.title: Needs a capable machine
points.text: JetBrains lists a 4-core x64 or Arm64 CPU, 8 GB of RAM and 10 GB of disk as the minimum. The Linux Flatpak alone is about 2 GB.

points.title: Windows has the most choice
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 84 versions, for x64 and Arm64, installable per user or for the whole machine. macOS lists only the current release, for Intel and Apple silicon on macOS 12 or later.

points.title: Linux Flatpak runs behind
points.text: The Linux build here is a Flathub package for x64 and Arm64 that Flathub does not mark as verified, and it sits at 2025.3.3 while Windows and Mac are on 2026 releases. JetBrains also offers its own Linux download, a snap and the Toolbox App, which keeps the IDE updated.
